page: Vultr voc-s-1c-8gb-150s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring a single dedicated AMD EPYC physical core running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. This server is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage is provided by a 150 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, though it lacks hyper-threading.

In benchmark evaluations, the single-core dedicated CPU demonstrates top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core tests, placing in the top 10%. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks also show strong results, with gzip compression reaching 31.57 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.38 GB/sec. However, the single-core limitation results in weak multi-core CPU performance and poor PassMark physics scores. Memory bandwidth is average for large blocks at 40.43 GB/sec read and 36.8 GB/sec write, but cached small-block read bandwidth is weak at 165.43 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated CPU resources, making it a viable option for workloads requiring guaranteed single-core compute performance without the overhead of shared-core environments. The bundled 150 GB NVMe SSD provides substantial local storage density relative to the single vCPU. It is best suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight database operations, basic text and image manipulation, and low-traffic web serving where multi-core scaling is not a primary requirement.
